title: SLO-aware adaptive inference recommendations (draft)
content:
Purpose
--------
This is a working draft capturing recommended defaults and spreadsheet layouts for a SLO-aware, adaptive inference optimization strategy. The goal is to produce a single source-of-truth that product, infra, and serving runtime teams can use to: 1) estimate per-route unit economics, 2) pick conservative batching/caching/quantization defaults, and 3) define safe rollout/fallback rules for production.

Summary recommendations (high level)
----------------------------------
- Introduce per-route SLO profiles (latency target, p95 target, quality budget). Use these to pick batching windows, max batch size, and cache policies.
- Default quantization profiles by model family (conservative -> aggressive) and tie them to an automated quality check (eval harness) before traffic rollout.
- Use an "effective cost" column in the cost model spreadsheet that accounts for batching efficiency and cache token savings so product owners can compare configurations easily.
- Provide a small number (3) of named presets for customers: "Low-latency chat", "Throughput-first embeddings", "Balanced (general)". Presets map to concrete spreadsheet parameter values.

Key spreadsheet design (opt-cost-v2)
-----------------------------------
Suggested file name: opt_cost_model_v2.xlsx (tabbed workbook: routes, models, presets, eval-results, run-history)
Columns for routes tab (all columns plain strings or numbers):
- route_id (string)
- route_description (string)
- model_family (string)
- default_model_version (string)
- avg_tokens_per_request (number)
- base_latency_ms (number) // median cold-start latency at batch=1, no cache
- p95_latency_ms (number) // measured at current config
- desired_p95_ms (number) // SLO
- workload_archetype (string) // e.g., chat-low-latency, embed-high-throughput, batch-inference
- max_batch_size (number)
- batching_window_ms (number)
- batching_efficiency_factor (decimal) // modeled fraction of token amortization (0-1)
- cache_prefix_enabled (yes/no)
- cache_ttl_s (number)
- expected_cache_hit_rate (decimal)
- token_savings_per_hit (number)
- quant_profile (string) // e.g., fp16, q4f16, int8-dynamic
- quality_regression_pct (decimal) // measured drop vs baseline (percent)
- fallback_model (string)
- estimated_per_request_cost_usd (number)
- effective_per_token_cost_usd (number)
- notes (string)

Formulas (text description)
- effective_per_token_cost = base_per_token_cost / (1 + batching_gain + cache_token_savings)
  - batching_gain approximated as: batching_efficiency_factor * (max_batch_size - 1) / max_batch_size
  - cache_token_savings = expected_cache_hit_rate * token_savings_per_hit / avg_tokens_per_request
- estimated_per_request_cost = effective_per_token_cost * avg_tokens_per_request + overhead_per_request

Preset defaults (recommended starting values)
- Low-latency chat
  - desired_p95_ms: 120
  - max_batch_size: 4
  - batching_window_ms: 10
  - batching_efficiency_factor: 0.15
  - cache_prefix_enabled: yes (short ttl)
  - cache_ttl_s: 20
  - expected_cache_hit_rate: 0.05
  - quant_profile: fp16 (no quantization by default)
  - fallback_model: same-family smaller model

- Throughput-first embeddings
  - desired_p95_ms: 1000 (soft)
  - max_batch_size: 256
  - batching_window_ms: 200
  - batching_efficiency_factor: 0.65
  - cache_prefix_enabled: no (usually not helpful for embeddings)
  - quant_profile: q4f16 or int8-dynamic (aggressive)
  - expected_cache_hit_rate: 0.0

- Balanced (general purpose)
  - desired_p95_ms: 300
  - max_batch_size: 32
  - batching_window_ms: 50
  - batching_efficiency_factor: 0.35
  - cache_prefix_enabled: yes
  - cache_ttl_s: 120
  - expected_cache_hit_rate: 0.12
  - quant_profile: q4f16 (moderate)

Quantization guidance (policy + rollout)
---------------------------------------
- Quant profiles are per-model-family. Suggested tiering:
  - conservative: fp16 (baseline)
  - moderate: q4f16 (good cost/quality tradeoff for many LLaMA-like families)
  - aggressive: int8-dynamic (best cost, higher risk of subtle quality drift)
- For each model_family + quant_profile, require a small eval suite (10-20 prompts representative of customer workloads) producing: BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics where applicable and a human/QC pass rate.
- Define a quality_regression_pct threshold (default 1.5%). If quantization causes > threshold regression on eval set, block automatic rollout.
- Fallback logic: if quantized model fails quality checks in production (monitored by production eval p95 of similarity score or alerts from quality monitors), automatically route to next-safe profile (e.g., fp16).

Caching rules and heuristics
---------------------------
- Two cache types: prefix-response cache (short TTL) and embedding cache (long TTL). Tune per-route.
- Prefix cache good for structured prompts or high-reuse system messages; set TTL conservatively (20-120s) and monitor freshness regressions.
- Expected_cache_hit_rate should be measured from a sample trace – do not guess. If <3%, disable cache for the route.
- For embedding-heavy routes, maintain an LRU cache with explicit keying (user_id + vector_key) and monitor semantic drift.

Adaptive routing heuristics (SLO-aware)
--------------------------------------
- If p95 for route exceeds desired_p95_ms, degrade non-critical requests first:
  - apply smaller batching window to reduce latency (reduce batching_window_ms by 50%)
  - reduce max_batch_size by 50% for a cooldown period (30s)
  - if still violating, fallback to a lower-cost model or change quant_profile to a lower-latency profile (e.g., fp16)
- Use weighted priority queues so background/bulk requests are batched aggressively while foreground requests get preferential small batches.

Example row (text CSV)
route_id,route_description,model_family,avg_tokens_per_request,base_latency_ms,p95_latency_ms,desired_p95_ms,max_batch_size,batching_window_ms,expected_cache_hit_rate,token_savings_per_hit,quant_profile,estimated_per_request_cost_usd
chat-small,In-app chat with short context,redwood-chat-7b,80,45,150,120,4,10,0.06,30,fp16,0.0024
embed-bulk,Bulk embedding upload,redwood-embed-12b,1024,1200,1600,1000,256,200,0.0,0,q4f16,0.0009

Quality monitoring and eval integration
--------------------------------------
- Link each route to an eval suite id in the spreadsheet (eval-results tab). Record baseline metrics and store historical comparisons (run-history tab).
- Alerting thresholds: if production similarity score or judge pass rate drops by >1.5% vs baseline for 10min window, trigger automatic rollback/fallback and create pager alert (severity P2).

Operational runbook snippets (short)
----------------------------------
- On rollout of a new quant_profile: start 2% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated eval check at each step. If quality_regression_pct > threshold, immediately revert and route to rollback model.
- Batching changes: allow hot-reload of batching_window_ms and max_batch_size. When increasing batching aggressiveness, stage changes during off-peak and monitor p95.

Open questions / tradeoffs
-------------------------
- How to quantify human-visible quality regressions for chat beyond simple metrics? Need a small human-in-the-loop evaluation plan per model_family.
- What is a safe default quality_regression_pct for enterprise customers vs self-serve free tier? Suggest 1% enterprise, 2% self-serve for initial defaults.
- Should cache keys be provided as first-class route config in the Console? (pros: safer, cons: more surface area)

Next steps / action items
------------------------
- Priya (APPLIED ML): create 3 eval suites (chat-short, chat-long, embeddings-bulk) and attach eval IDs to the spreadsheet. Due: 2025-11-19.
- Infra (Jamal): add telemetry fields for batching_efficiency_factor and token_savings_per_hit to the route metrics pipeline. Due: 2025-11-10 (high priority).
- DevEx (Sofie): draft Console UI mockups for per-route presets and an "apply preset" flow. Due: 2025-11-24.
- Product (Elliot): consolidate presets into opt_cost_model_v2.xlsx and circulate to owners. Due: 2025-11-12.

Notes / rough ideas (scratch)
----------------------------
- Consider adding a small synthetic load test harness that can approximate batching efficiency by replaying traffic with different batching_window_ms to estimate real-world batching_gain.
- We might want to expose an "economics slider" in Console that shows estimated monthly savings when switching presets (assumes monthly QPS from billing data).

References / links
------------------
- Confluence: OPT-6782 (design notes)
- GitHub PR: repo/pull/842 (quant profile rollout code)
- JIRA: OPT-345 (spreadsheet consolidation), INFRA-1297 (metrics additions)

This is intentionally rough — please add model-specific numbers into the spreadsheet and run a small A/B rollout on one customer route before recommending defaults more broadly.
